topic: Your end-of-workday shutdown: the drive home (animated carousel, native style, research-led)
caption:
Logged off at five, still at work in your head at nine?

Switching off from work in your own time can be learnt. A review of programs for working adults found they helped people do it, on average. The most helpful ones worked on boundaries between work and home, handling the feelings work leaves behind, and sleep. Longer programs helped more than very short ones.

A small end-of-workday routine is one place to start: write tomorrow's to-do list, do one small closing act, and pick a time when work messages wait. The first two are examples the researchers give, not tested one by one. These were studies of employees in general, not people with burnout.

And if the workload itself is too much, a routine won't fix that. That part sits with the workplace too.

Save this for 5pm.

Sources:
Karabinski, T., Haun, V. C., Nübold, A., Wendsche, J., & Wegge, J. (2021). Interventions for improving psychological detachment from work: A meta-analysis. Journal of Occupational Health Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/ocp0000280
Demerouti, E. (2024). Burnout: A comprehensive review. Zeitschrift für Arbeitswissenschaft. https://doi.org/10.1007/s41449-024-00452-3
